findings.claim: The diff for the focused-agent-skills target contains substantial unrelated content (MCP 2026-07-28 stateless HTTP contract, rmcp 3.1.4 upgrade, compass-partition extraction, COMPASS_MAX_GRAPH_BYTES, chunk-streaming reads), breaching the no-unrelated-diff-noise constraint.
findings.evidence: Constraint: 'git diff and git status --short contain no unrelated or generated noise'. The packet target is 'focused-agent-skills', yet the CHANGELOG hunk adds eight entries with no relation to skills, COMPATIBILITY.md gains entire 'MCP HTTP compatibility' and 'MCP structured result compatibility' sections, and docs/reference/commands.md gains a `compass serve` paragraph about `--session-timeout` deprecation. verification.md itself admits prior packets were 'repository-wide cumulative diff'; this packet still carries those cumulative hunks.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the MCP, partition, and graph-size doc/changelog hunks into their own changes so this diff contains only focused-agent-skills content.

findings.claim: Acceptance criterion 3.1 is checked complete and claims 'rollback regressions' were added, but the diff contains no test that injects a mid-install failure and verifies the full seven-skill collection is restored, even though the rollback path was materially changed (conditional restore replaced by unconditional restore_transaction over the new SkillCollectionSnapshot).
findings.evidence: tasks.md 3.1: '[x] Add trigger-discrimination, complete-tree, checksum, idempotence, multi-consumer, conflict, and rollback regressions.' The new tests in the diff are the trigger-corpus unit test, install_preflights_unowned_focused_skill_before_mutation (fails before any mutation, so it exercises no rollback), and uninstall_preserves_a_modified_focused_skill. Meanwhile execute_skill_target now calls restore_transaction unconditionally on install_skill_at_scoped failure ('let rollback = restore_transaction(&skill_snapshot, &adapter_snapshots);'), replacing the prior conditional that skipped restore when staging failed before mutation — exactly the behavior a rollback regression should pin down.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that forces install_skill_package_at_scoped to fail after at least one sibling has been activated (e.g., via an unwritable focused destination that passes preflight or a fault-injecting hook) and asserts all seven destinations and adapter files are byte-identical to their pre-install state; or uncheck 3.1.

findings.claim: contains_windows_absolute_path matches URI schemes, so any future 'https://' or 'http://' link in a focused skill will fail the release build misreported as an absolute Windows path.
findings.evidence: The check is `window[0].is_ascii_alphabetic() && window[1] == b':' && matches!(window[2], b'\\' | b'/')`; in "https://example.com" the window ['s', ':', '/'] satisfies all three conditions. validate_portable_paths runs this over every focused SKILL.md body, and compass-mcp-setup is precisely the skill most likely to gain a documentation URL later. The build gate would then fail with 'focused skill contains an absolute Windows path marker', a misleading diagnostic.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude the '://' form (e.g., require the character before the drive letter to be absent or non-alphanumeric, or reject only when window[2] == b'\\' or the colon is not followed by '//'), and add a unit case asserting contains_windows_absolute_path("https://example.com") is false.
